# HexaLoam

> HexaLoam is an open-source, fully 3D-printable hexapod robot (hexabot) with native editable SOLIDWORKS CAD. It has 18 joints (3 per leg) driven by 36 MG996R servos, an integrated RP-Lidar (2D) mount, MATLAB Simscape Multibody and URDF models, four controller configurations (Arduino Mega, ESP32, Raspberry Pi with 1 or 2 ESP32), firmware, and a Raspberry Pi Python and ROS 2 controller. MIT license, author "HexaLoam contributors".

## Who it fits

- Graduation and thesis projects that need an editable SOLIDWORKS hexapod with MATLAB simulation files and a fully printable body from cheap servos.
- Agricultural scouting and plant-inspection prototypes (greenhouse or crop row), once a camera mount and vision software are added; see the guide below.
- Education (gait, kinematics, torque analysis) and legged-robot research.

## Key facts

- Structure: 5 STL designs = 20 PLA+ printed pieces (chassis, 6x L1, 6x L2, 6x L3, LiDAR cover); 1.306 kg as sliced in Bambu Studio, supports excluded. CAD formats: SOLIDWORKS (Full_Robot_Assembly.SLDASM, LegMates.SLDASM), STEP, STL, 3MF, GLB.
- Actuation: 18 joints, 36 MG996R servos, two back-to-back per joint with mirrored angles (MA2 = 3000 - MA1 microseconds). 2.157 N.m stall per joint at 6.0 V.
- Sensing: RP-Lidar (2D) mount and cover in the chassis CAD. 2D SLAM (for example slam_toolbox) is what this lidar supports; "LOAM" in the name is not a claim of 3D LOAM odometry.
- MATLAB: Simscape Multibody XML export + STEP, single-leg static study, gait trajectory replay, URDF for importrobot.
- Electronics: controller configurations A (Arduino Mega), B (ESP32 + 2x PCA9685), C (Raspberry Pi + 1 ESP32), D (Raspberry Pi + 2 ESP32); 15 wiring diagrams; 3S 5000 mAh LiPo.
- Testing: tested in four controller configurations (A-D) by simulation parameters and analysis of mass versus required torque. Total mass 3.79-4.02 kg. Wave (45-48% of stall) and ripple (59-62%) stay within the 70% continuous limit; tripod needs 81-86%.

## Honest limitations

- No camera mount in the CAD and no plant-vision code yet.
- The Simscape import has 29 extra 6-DOF joints from missing CAD mates; use the URDF as the clean 18-joint kinematic model.
- URDF and Gazebo dynamics are not verified against hardware.
- Physical bench and field tests are pending; mass and torque figures are analytical estimates.
- MG996R hobby servos limit continuous load and rough-terrain use.
